subject.title: fix(sessions): reconcile client-abandoned running sessions on restart

question: Should this PR adopt rotation-time eviction as the shared ownership boundary for embedded and reply registries after focused live restart proof and CI-failure resolution?
rationale: This is a cross-registry session-state and availability decision affecting process-global owners during gateway restart; the supplied test claims do not independently establish the full operational behavior.

options.title: Require focused restart proof and green CI
options.body: Capture a redacted real gateway run where a client abandons a running session, SIGUSR1 rotates the lifecycle, recovery marks the orphan failed, and a current replacement remains live.

options.title: Accept the unit-test-only evidence
options.body: Merge based on the existing suite claims while accepting that the end-to-end restart ordering has not been demonstrated.

options.title: Pause for a narrower ownership design
options.body: Defer the PR if maintainers do not want lifecycle rotation to synchronously own registry eviction across these runtimes.

recommendation.title: Require focused restart proof and green CI
recommendation.body: Capture a redacted real gateway run where a client abandons a running session, SIGUSR1 rotates the lifecycle, recovery marks the orphan failed, and a current replacement remains live.

likelyOwner.reason: The author is assigned and owns the proposed lifecycle boundary; broader current-main ownership could not be verified here.
